key_insight: An agent-guided experimental workflow can be transferred and refined across different quantum processors to reliably execute the same quantum task despite hardware differences and drift.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to scale quantum experimentation beyond hand-tuned, device-specific procedures by combining automated decision-making with human operator intervention.
method: Developed the strategy on one three-qubit NMR processor and deployed it sequentially on four others.
Used an agent to evaluate evidence, choose the next measurements, and adapt procedures.
Combined device-specific calibration, control-pulse optimization, and measurement for three-qubit Grover state preparation.
evidence_signal: Across four processors, the reconstructed dominant eigenstates had marked-state populations from 0.910 to 0.959, with relative deviations below 3.8% from the ideal 0.945.
watch_item: The approach still depends on operator-side instrument preparation and physical intervention, so full autonomy and broader hardware transferability remain limited.
paper_title: Agent-assisted experimental strategy transfer across quantum processors
